Net a slight up lean: p_up 54 on an abs move of 15 gives +1.2. The findings sum (+2.1) is larger because the positioning and licensing items are each sized on their own; the gap is the unresolved royalty-durability question, which is the item most likely to set the sign.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is already pre-announced at >$186.4m (>30% sequential on $143.4m, raised 2026-09-21 from ~10% to >20% and again 2026-09-30 to >30%, both on VPD royalties), and consensus revenue $187.0-187.2m sits on that floor. The increment over the original ~10% guide (~$158m incl. $5m royalty) is ~$28m+ of royalty at near-100% margin. A rough walk (product ~$152m at ~53-54% GM, royalty ~$33m+, opex ~$40-45m, ~4.5m interest) gives roughly $1.35-1.60 EPS depending on tax, against the $1.27-1.32 consensus: a modest EPS beat is more likely than a miss, but the revenue line is known.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): revenue $143.4m vs $138.4m and EPS $1.04 vs $0.65, a 60% EPS beat, and the stock fell 7.05% on a conservative licensing outlook. This name has sold a large reported-quarter beat when the forward licensing line disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue is fully priced: the guide was public and consensus moved onto it. The EPS consensus ($1.27-1.32) may not carry the full royalty margin; if it did, estimates would sit nearer $1.45+. The EPS walk is my own arithmetic, not a document.
findings.independence: Same guidance release family as the finviz copy (https://finviz.com/news/397273/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance); consensus from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-vicor-vicr-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/). The margin walk uses Q2 call numbers (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1923044-20260722).

findings.finding: The Q4 guide risk is the durability of the Q3 royalty. On the Q2 call the prior $60m two-year license was scheduled at $5m of revenue in Q3, then $10m a quarter. The Q3 jump of ~$28m+ came from the first non-exclusive VPD license (announced 2026-09-16, terms undisclosed) and may include catch-up royalties on past unlicensed purchases. The company's own FY2026 floor (>$600m) implies only ≥$157m in Q4 against a Q3 of ≥$186m, while Q4 EPS consensus ($1.27) is flat with Q3. A sequential-down or royalty-normalising Q4 guide would land against a consensus that extrapolates Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The licensing/guide line set the sign on the last two prints with full detail: Q2 2026 -7.05% on a conservative licensing outlook despite a big beat; Q3 2025 +30.33% on the AI/licensing outlook. Guidance raises intra-quarter bought +9.9% (2026-09-22) and +11% after hours (2026-09-30).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 36% drawdown from the Oct 2 high may already discount a royalty that does not recur. If it were fully priced, Q4 EPS consensus would sit below Q3's rather than flat at $1.27 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VICR/earnings-forecasts). Whether the Q3 royalty is a catch-up is unknown; the 2026-09-30 release does not say (https://finviz.com/news/397273/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance).
findings.independence: Simply Wall St (2026-10-10) also calls royalty durability across coming quarters the near-term question (https://www.webull.com/news/15721832301667328). This is my inference from the Q2 call schedule and the FY floor, not a company statement about Q4.

findings.finding: The licensing pipeline is moving faster than the company guided. On the Q2 call (2026-07-21) management said new licenses 'may not result until our second ITC case gets to its final determination in 2027'. By 2026-09-21 the CEO said four OEMs and hyperscalers had licensed, some approaching Vicor after systems with allegedly infringing modules faced import restrictions, and that licenses were available early 'at a low royalty rate'. On 2026-10-09 the USITC instituted 337-TA-1526 on Vicor's '734 VPD patent against Delta, Infineon, Luxshare, MPS, Flex, Celestica, Quanta, Hon Hai and Ingrasys, seeking a limited exclusion order. That is leverage for more licensees, and the call (or a new licensee in the release) can raise the licensing outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Licensing news has been bought every time it was new: +~11% on the first VPD license (2026-09-17), +9.9% pre-market on the 2026-09-21 raise, +11% after hours on 2026-09-30. The ITC institution (2026-10-09) bought nothing visible; the stock kept falling with the sector.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock now trades below its pre-license level (~$216 on 2026-09-17; spot $197.70), so the market is valuing the licensing program at about zero incremental value despite four licensees and a newly instituted ITC case. If it were priced, the shares would hold some of the September licensing gains.
findings.independence: USITC institution notice, 337-TA-1526, 2026-10-09 (https://www.usitc.gov/sites/default/files/secretary/fed_reg_notices/337/337_1526_notice10092026sgl.pdf; release https://www.usitc.gov/press_room/news_release/2026/er1009_69342.htm), a different source from the company. The '2027' line is from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1923044-20260722).

findings.finding: The stock has fallen from ~$308.59 (2026-10-01) to $197.70 (2026-10-19), -36%, including -23.8% in five sessions, while the company raised its Q3 guide. The selloff coincides with a sector rout: Nasdaq -2.15% on 2026-10-16 and -4.48% for the week, SOXX -4.14% on 'AI-financing worries' around neoclouds. The beta is 2.37 and no company-specific negative was found (MarketBeat on the 2026-10-15 -10.5% day: no cause; volume ~80% below average). The 25d skew is call-bid at -5.5 vol points. Positioning into the print is washed out rather than crowded long.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In seven prints the stock rose five times; the median absolute reaction is 16.55%. The one large negative (2025-04-29, -23.1%) and Q2 2026 (-7.05%) both followed run-ups, not a drawdown of this size.
findings.why_not_priced: This item is the price. The claim is that the drawdown reflects sector de-risking and a run-up unwind (Quiver, 2026-10-08) rather than a known company negative. If a company-level negative existed, it would show in the news flow, analyst cuts or Form 8-Ks; none did. Analyst actions in the window were upgrades and target raises (Needham to $350 on 10-01, Zacks to Strong Buy on 10-01).

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is a widely read print, and the sector fell after it on financing worries. It is filed as a small proxy because it contradicts the demand-fear reading of the drawdown, not because anyone missed it.
